summary: The change moves the TypeScript declaration emit for the `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` entry out of its own tsup DTS pass and into the main dual-format config, so the wasm-inline declarations share the column-class declaration chunk with `./eql/v3` and `./adapter-kit`. That turns cross-entry schema authoring (a wasm-inline-authored table passed to `encryptedSupabase`, Drizzle, Prisma Next or the native `Encryption`, and vice versa) from a compile error into valid TypeScript. JS emission is unchanged: both configs keep their JS entry lists, so runtime behaviour, encryption and payloads are not touched, and the runtime paths that consume schemas already probe structurally. The rest is a new dist-level type gate (run in CI via test:types:dist), tightened test assertions, comment edits, a CI-only hard failure for an unbuilt logger gate, deletion of a docs guard that asserted the old compile error, and rewritten customer-shipped skills that now recommend sharing one schema module across entries. The material risks are a mis-shaped published `dist/wasm-inline.d.ts` (irreversible once published, but gated) and shipped guidance that overstates where cross-entry sharing works (version skew, CommonJS projects). Both are loud (compile or load errors), not silent. Verdict: focused review of the emitted declaration surface and the skill wording.

behaviour_changes.description: `dist/wasm-inline.d.ts` is now produced by the main config's DTS pass (dts.entry = mainEntry + src/wasm-inline.ts) instead of the wasm-inline config's own pass (now dts: false). Its column-class declarations come from the shared chunk, so a wasm-inline table and an eql/v3 table are the same TypeScript type. The main pass is dual-format, so an unreferenced `dist/wasm-inline.d.cts` also ships.

Type-level contract of the `./wasm-inline` export widens: tables authored from it are assignable to `AnyV3Table` from `./eql/v3` and accepted by every first-party adapter's `schemas`, and native-authored tables are accepted by the WASM `Encryption`. JS entry lists for both configs are unchanged, so emitted runtime code is not changed by this diff.

Customer-shipped skills (stash-edge, stash-supabase, stash-managed-platforms, stash-encryption) reverse their guidance: from 'schema modules do not cross entries, author from eql/v3 for the Supabase adapter' to 'one schema module serves both entries; either import works', with a note to upgrade if the old diagnostic appears.

Adds dist-level type gates (dist-types/wasm-inline-type-identity.ts, node16/wasm-inline.mts cross-entry probes); deletes scripts/__tests__/skills-supabase-edge-schema-entry.test.mjs, which forbade the now-recommended pairing in shipped docs; pins the supabase domain-mismatch error message; makes logger-edge-safety throw at module scope in CI when dist/ is missing instead of skipping.
The Supabase adapter's v2-table error message now names `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` as a valid authoring entry alongside `eql/v3`. Text only; branching is unchanged.

failure_scenarios.title: Published dist/wasm-inline.d.ts differs from the previous surface for edge consumers
failure_scenarios.trigger: The main config's dual-format DTS rollup emits wasm-inline declarations that differ from the old standalone pass (for example a wasm-only type moved to or renamed inside a shared chunk, a declaration resolved differently under the main config, or chunk references that do not resolve in the tarball).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Before, `dist/wasm-inline.d.ts` was a self-contained rollup from its own pass. Now it comes from the main config's pass (tsup.config.ts:52) alongside ten other entries and references shared declaration chunks, while the wasm config emits JS only (tsup.config.ts:78). Any difference in exported names or shapes reaches every Workers/Deno/Bun/Supabase Edge TypeScript consumer of `./wasm-inline`.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Type errors or missing exports for edge TypeScript users after upgrading a patch release. Runtime is unaffected. A published release cannot be withdrawn, so a fix needs a new release.

failure_scenarios.title: Shipped skills promise cross-entry schema sharing where it still fails (version skew, CommonJS projects)
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer's coding agent follows the updated skill while the installed @cipherstash/stack predates this fix (skills ship in the separately installed `stash` tarball), or while their Node server compiles or runs as CommonJS.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The skills now say one schema.ts can serve a Node server and an Edge Function in both directions. `./wasm-inline` has only an `import` branch, so a CommonJS server cannot load a schema module that imports it. Under node16 resolution, CommonJS resolves `./eql/v3` and `./v3` to the separately emitted `.d.cts` declarations, which do not share identity with the ESM `.d.ts` set. On older stack versions the old TS2322 still occurs. The text-level guard that policed these snippets was deleted, and nothing type-checks the skills.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A customer's build fails with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM or TS2322 after following first-party guidance. An agent may 'fix' it with `as any`, which the skills themselves warn against. Loud, not silent: no wrong data or plaintext path, because runtime detection is structural.

evidence.claim: Main config emits declarations for mainEntry plus src/wasm-inline.ts: `dts: { entry: [...mainEntry, 'src/wasm-inline.ts'] }`.
The wasm-inline config still emits ESM JS for the same entry, but with `dts: false`.
mainEntry holds the same ten JS entries the base config listed inline, so JS emission is unchanged.
`./wasm-inline` exports only an `import` branch with types at ./dist/wasm-inline.d.ts (no require branch).
New gate asserts a wasm-inline table and column are assignable to AnyV3Table from dist/eql/v3, and that tables cross both Encryption clients in both directions, resolving ../dist by relative path.
Node16-mode gate asserts the same cross-entry identity by package name through the exports map (ESM only).
CI runs `turbo run test:types:dist --filter @cipherstash/stack`, which per package.json:201 runs tsc over both dist-types tsconfigs.
isV3ColumnLike detects v3 columns structurally (getName/getEqlType/getQueryCapabilities/build), so runtime handling of cross-entry tables does not depend on class identity.
Skill now states 'One schema module serves both entries' and 'pass the result to either client'.
Skill states either entry may author the table for encryptedSupabase, with an upgrade note if TS2322 appears.
Managed-platforms skill now says either entry may author encryptedSupabase schemas.
Skill states one schema.ts can serve a Node server and an Edge Function, in both directions.
The diff removes the 'Schema Modules Do Not Cross Entries' section and its 'keep two schema modules' advice.
Deleted guard documented that skills ship in the stash tarball and are not type-checked, and failed on any shipped snippet pairing the Supabase wasm-inline adapter with wasm-inline-authored schemas.
Assertion now pins the full domain-mismatch message emitted by verify.ts:59.
When dist/adapter-kit.js is missing and CI is set, the test file throws at module scope instead of skipping.
The v2-table error message now also names @cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline. Text-only change.
Drizzle stores the column builder under `Symbol.for('cipherstash:eqlv3Column')`, which is realm-global rather than per bundle copy.
No instanceof check against a column or table class exists in any package source at head.
Skills are copied into the stash and wizard tarballs and into customer repositories by stash init; nothing type-checks them.
CommonJS resolution takes the require branch (*.d.cts), which tsup emits in a separate declaration pass from the ESM *.d.ts set.
Neither node_modules nor a built dist/ exists in the checkout, so a build or test run was not possible offline.
